variants.note: the strong form, used when the word is stressed or said alone

pronunciation.notes: **An** is normally unstressed, *ən*, and used directly before a vowel sound (*an apple*, *an hour*); before a consonant sound, **a** is used instead (*a book*). The strong form, *æn*, is used when the word is stressed or said alone.

core_idea: **An** is the form of **a** used directly before a word that begins with a vowel sound; it introduces a person or thing as one example of its kind, without pointing to a particular, already-known one.

senses.definition: used before a singular countable noun beginning with a vowel sound, to talk about a person or thing without saying which one, especially the first time it is mentioned
senses.explanation: **An** is simply **a** used before a vowel sound: *I saw an owl in the garden*. Once the thing has been introduced this way, **the** usually takes over the next time it is mentioned: *I saw an owl; the owl was gray*.

examples.text: I saw an owl in the garden last night.
She works as an editor at a small company.
There's an email for you from Yuki.

compare.note: **a** is used instead directly before a consonant sound
**the** is used instead once the listener already knows which one is meant

senses.definition: used before a singular countable noun beginning with a vowel sound to make a general statement about every member of a kind
senses.explanation: This use talks about the whole kind, not one particular example: *an elephant never forgets* means every elephant.

examples.text: An honest answer is always better than a clever excuse.
An umbrella is useful on a rainy day.

senses.definition: used after a number or amount and before a noun of time or measurement beginning with a vowel sound, to mean each or every
senses.explanation: This use gives a rate: how often, how much, or how fast something happens: *fifty miles an hour*, *once an evening*.

examples.text: The car was going almost eighty miles an hour.
Ravi checks his phone about once an hour.
The parking garage charges five dollars an hour.

synonym_discrimination.note: **An** and **a** are the same word. Use **an** directly before a vowel sound, whatever the spelling: *an hour*, *an MBA*, *an X-ray*; use **a** before a consonant sound: *a university*, *a one-time offer*, *a UFO*.

usage_note: Before an abbreviation or a letter said on its own, the choice still follows the sound of the first letter's name, not its spelling: *an SOS*, *an MP*, *an FAQ*, but *a UN report*, *a European visa*.

learner_errors.note: **Honest** begins with a vowel sound, since the **h** is silent, so **an** is used, not **a**.

learner_errors.incorrect: I saw an university on my way to work.
learner_errors.correct: I saw a university on my way to work.
learner_errors.note: **University** begins with a consonant sound, **y**, even though its first letter is a vowel, so **a** is used, not **an**.

learner_errors.incorrect: I'll be there in an hour and an half.
learner_errors.correct: I'll be there in an hour and a half.
learner_errors.note: **Hour** begins with a silent **h**, so **an** is used; **half** begins with a pronounced **h**, so **a** is used.

adaptation.grammar: **An** is simply **a** used before a vowel sound; the choice depends on pronunciation, not spelling (*an hour*, but *a university*, *a one-way street*).
adaptation.pronunciation: **An** is normally unstressed, *ən*; the strong form *æn* is used only when the word is stressed or said alone.
